A_MY_MEDIAN_CLAIM_WAS_FALSE.I_verified_it: confirmed. The identity holds only for ODD n, where the median IS an order statistic. At EVEN n the median averages the two middle values, and averaging does not commute with reciprocation. Our design is 30 pairs per contrast -- EVEN -- so it fails exactly where I applied it.
A_MY_MEDIAN_CLAIM_WAS_FALSE.I_wrote: 'for positive values median(1/X) = 1/median(X) exactly', and used it to argue T1 and T2 could share one measurement set because their C statistics would be reciprocals by construction.
A_MY_MEDIAN_CLAIM_WAS_FALSE.consequence: the argument for sharing T1/T2 measurements collapses. Root independently ordered separate measurements, so the plan changes for two reasons, not one.
A_MY_MEDIAN_CLAIM_WAS_FALSE.root_counterexample: 15 values of 1 and 15 values of 4 give median 2.5, whose reciprocal is 0.4; the median of the reciprocals is 0.625.
A_MY_MEDIAN_CLAIM_WAS_FALSE.root_further: 'Compute the declared median statistics directly; do not change the estimator to manufacture reciprocity.' Adopted: C is computed from its own paired and solo medians per contrast, and no reciprocal relationship is assumed or asserted.

C is defined as a ratio candidate/incumbent, and for positive values median(1/X) = 1/median(X) exactly, so computing both C's from ONE measurement set forces C_T1 = 1 / C_T2 as an algebraic identity.
T1_and_T2_share_one_measurement_set_AND_.protocol_is_silent: 5.8(4) says 'for each of the four contrasts' and does not say whether T1 and T2 may share a measurement set.

T1_and_T2_share_one_measurement_set_AND_.what_could_make_them_genuinely_differ: slot/position asymmetry. A pair assigns arms to positions 1 and 2, and if side-by-side latency depends on slot, then running the pair with the roles exchanged is a DIFFERENT measurement, not the same one inverted.
T1_and_T2_share_one_measurement_set_AND_.why_that_is_uncomfortable: two contrasts would then carry compression statistics that are exact reciprocals by construction rather than by measurement. If the protocol intends them as independent empirical quantities, they must be measured separately.

load_coverage_rule.a_request_is_not_proof: a submitted HTTP request alone does not prove inference is active; the server-side active/processing observation used must be defined. Point samples before and after cannot by themselves prove no interior gap.
load_coverage_rule.gap_between_attempts: ALLOWED. Stop dispatching, let the controlled load restart, resume only once activity is evidenced. A predetermined scheduling rule, not a failed check.
load_coverage_rule.gap_intersecting_a_running_check: that preparation check is INVALID: retain the timing and result, stop for diagnosis, do NOT exclude the task as a scientific reference failure, do NOT retry until favourable, do NOT alter the reference threshold.
load_coverage_rule.my_earlier_default_was_stricter_and_wron: I had proposed a hard stop on the FIRST gap of any kind. Root distinguishes gaps BETWEEN attempts (schedule around them) from gaps INTERSECTING a check (invalidate that check). The distinction is what makes a 2,260-attempt sweep feasible at all.
load_coverage_rule.no_hiding: single prescribed coder load at max_tokens 1024; extra concurrency must not be used to mask gaps. EOS, failures, restart gaps, abandoned requests and unknown usage all stay in the load ledger.
per_attempt_record: monotonic start and end times on the same host clock
the load-window identifiers covering that entire interval
load_coverage_rule.resolved_by_root_2005: PER-ATTEMPT coverage, evidenced by REUSABLE load windows. A new load request or metrics scrape per verifier attempt is NOT required; one generation's observed active interval may cover several checks.
load_coverage_rule.sampled_only: if the server exposes only sampled activity, that limitation is LABELLED and a concrete instrumentation proposal returned; continuous coverage is never asserted from interpolation.
